definition: Automatic Call Distributor. Telephony/omnichannel system that routes contacts to agents using skills/policies.
After‑Call Work. Post‑contact wrap time included in handle time and staffing assumptions.
Average Handle Time. Talk + hold + ACW per contact; a driver of workload and staffing.
Adaptation Latency. Median time from a material signal (campaign/outage/sentiment) to the effective routing/schedule change.
Experimental design comparing two conditions; often used for pilot rule toggles.
Automation Acceptance Rate. Accepted automated prompts ÷ eligible prompts.
Average Speed of Answer. Mean wait time for answered contacts; pairs with SL to show depth of delay.
Business Process Outsourcing; external vendor capacity used under guardrails or envelopes.
Business Intelligence; reporting/visualization layer aligned to the single source of truth.
Contact Center as a Service; cloud platform providing routing, reporting, and channels.
Customer Effort Score; perceived effort to resolve an issue.
Customer Lifetime Value; value contribution over a relationship horizon.
A defined population segment used for pilots and measurement (e.g., tenure band, skill).
Customer Relationship Management; system of record for customer interactions and attributes.
Customer Satisfaction; survey‑based outcome metric.
Lightweight documentation of automated or human decisions: inputs, owner, guardrails, rollback path.
Discrete‑Event Simulation. Event‑by‑event modeling of queues/skills/policies for planning and policy evaluation.
A probability band (e.g., P50/P80/P95) for staffing need; leaders pick a band that matches risk tolerance.
Share of intervals where realized need falls within the chosen band (e.g., P80).
Enterprise Resource Planning; finance/inventory backbone integrated with WFM decisions.
Extract–Transform–Load; data pipelines feeding planning and the ROC.
Employee Wellbeing Index. Composite (e.g., schedule stability, growth delivered, burnout risk).
Employee Experience; perceived quality of work environment and systems.
Share of automated decisions with recorded reasons, inputs, and override path.
Simple fairness lens comparing outcomes across cohorts (e.g., tenure/shift).
Visual showing a forecast median with widening percentile bands over time.
Managed repository of model features used consistently across training and inference.
First‑Contact Resolution; issue resolved in the first interaction.
Cadence that approves guardrails, rollbacks, and changes to formulas and rule logic.
Goals, Roles, Processes, Interpersonal, Technology. Five‑lens structure used in each level’s operational profile.
Policy bounds that define safe ranges (e.g., SL floor, occupancy band, fairness limits) for automation and people.
Human Resources Information System; authoritative staffing/tenure/attrition data.
One‑pager clarifying inputs/outputs/SLAs between teams/systems for an integration.
IT Service Management; incident/ticket framework mirrored in ROC incident handling.
Learning Management System; source for training content, delivery, and completion data.
(Mixed‑Integer) Linear Programming; optimization methods for schedules/assignments under constraints.
Mean Absolute Percentage Error; forecasting accuracy metric (sensitive to small denominators).
Lightweight model documentation (purpose, data, limits, monitoring).
Low‑latency inference tier that exposes models via stable APIs.
Sampling‑based method to produce distributions (not points) for plans and KPIs.
Net Promoter Score; “recommend” intent proxy.
Share of agent time engaged on work; manage via bands (e.g., 78–88%).
Value difference between static and flexible posture under uncertainty.
Overtime; scheduled or incidental work beyond base shift.
1-page scope/owners/metrics/rollback for a time-boxed pilot.
Quarterly cadence aligning outcomes to objectives; adjusts roadmap and ownership.
Declared coverage stance (e.g., P80 envelope) given risk tolerance and budget.
Nonlinear sensitivity of SL to small staffing changes in tight queues.
Roles for cadences: A — Accountable; R — Responsible; C — Consulted; I — Informed. Abbreviations used in this book: CWS, EAIG, ROC Lead, MLO.
Chief Workforce Strategist. Executive owner for workforce strategy and scorecards; co‑owns scenario/portfolio reviews; selects staffing posture by band.
Enterprise AI Governance. Cross‑functional oversight for explainability, fairness, drift, and rollbacks; chairs the governance review.
Operational owner of the Resource Optimization Center cadence; chairs daily stand‑ups; coordinates intraday moves across skills/sites.
Model Lifecycle Owner. Accountable for model deployment, monitoring, drift/rollback, and audit evidence; partner to EAIG.

Supervises intraday variance across queues; implements schedule/routing adjustments; manages incident response; and designs/tunes rules and automation with supervisors, WFM, and IT. Present from L2 (reactive) through L3–L5 (increasingly proactive).
Pattern for automation/playbooks: a rule with a condition and a specific action; not the RTA role.
Versioned inventory of rules with owner, intent, guardrails, metrics, and change history.
Weekly review of driver changes and updated weights that feed envelopes and rules.
Supervisor Coaching Ratio. Share of supervisor time on coaching vs.\ admin.
Timeliness promise (e.g., 80% in 30s) read at 15–30 minute intervals.
Link between employee experience, service quality, and financial performance.
Share of intervals where SL and ASA are within a published band.
Policy for ignoring abandons under a small wait threshold in SL math; document threshold.
Single Source of Truth; governed, versioned metric/data definitions.
Schedule Quality Index. Composite of lead time, change count, preference match, and stability.
Startup, Turnaround, Realignment, Sustaining Success—context lens for sequencing moves.
Time‑to‑Stabilize. Time from threshold breach to return within the service band.
Variance Capture Efficiency. Minutes redeployed to value work ÷ eligible micro‑availability minutes.
Structured record of incidents, causes, actions, and results that feeds weekly changes.
Voluntary Overtime; offered under guardrails when understaffed.
Voluntary Time Off; offered under guardrails when overstaffed.
Weighted Absolute Percentage Error; preferred for uneven interval volumes.
Workforce Management; the loop: forecast → schedule → real‑time → learn.
Five‑level progression (L1–L5) from manual foundations to enterprise orchestration.
